title: Minimal DPA for Early-Access Partner Integrations (Template)
content:
Purpose:
This is a streamlined Data Processing Addendum (DPA) intended for early-access partners integrating with Redwood Inference test endpoints or limited-production sandboxes. The goal is a minimal, pragmatic set of commitments to enable integrations quickly while preserving essential privacy and security controls. This document is a template and not the final executed DPA.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies only to Partner accounts marked as "early-access" in our provisioning system and to data sent to Redwood test or sandbox endpoints.
- Not intended for full production workloads handling regulated personal data unless expressly amended and signed.
- Where Partner escalates to Dedicated/Private, both parties must switch to the full standard DPA and supporting exhibits.

Definitions (short):
- Controller / Processor: follows standard meanings under applicable data protection law. Redwood is the Processor when processing on behalf of Partner.
- Personal Data: any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person.
- Sandbox Data: data routed to early-access/test endpoints; may include synthetic or obfuscated records.

Data types and permitted processing:
- Partner will indicate expected data classes at onboarding: "synthetic", "pseudonymized_personal", "personal".
- Redwood will only process the categories expressly permitted in the onboarding form and for the purposes of providing inference/hosting services, debugging, and integration support.

Security commitments (baseline for early-access):
- Encryption: Data in transit must use TLS 1.2+; sandbox endpoints enforce TLS. At-rest encryption provided for sandbox artifacts but may be ephemeral.
- Access controls: Role-based access for Redwood staff; privileged access is logged and justified by a ticket.
- Minimum controls: MFA for operator accounts, periodic credential rotation.
- Logging & retention: Integration logs retained for 30 days by default; partner may request extended retention with justification.

Subprocessors and limited subprocessing for early-access:
- Partner consents to Redwood engaging subprocessors for hosting, monitoring, and agenting infrastructure limited to sandbox operations.
- Redwood will provide a short list of subprocessors used for the early-access environment during onboarding and update the list on material changes.
- Partner may object to a subprocessor within 10 business days; continued objection triggers a review (not automatic termination).

Breach notification and escalation (accelerated):
- Redwood will notify Partner of confirmed or highly-likely security incidents affecting Partner Sandbox Data within 24 hours of internal detection.
- Initial notification: brief summary + mitigation steps in progress.
- Follow-up: detailed report within 7 calendar days if incident materially affects confidentiality or availability.
- For incidents limited to transient debug logs or synthetic records, Redwood will note severity and residual risk; full report if personal data impacted.

Data residency and segmentation options (early-access specific):
- Partner may request region pinning for sandbox traffic (e.g., eu-west1). We will honor region pinning where capacity exists; request may add lead time.
- Sandbox environments are logically segmented; not guaranteed physical isolation.

Key management and escrow (optional):
- For partners requiring greater isolation during early-access, Redwood can support customer-managed encryption keys (bring-your-own-key) for sandbox artifacts where feasible.
- Key escrow: if requested, Redwood will propose a simple escrow arrangement limited to rollback/incident response purposes; details escalated to legal.

Termination and data deletion:
- Either party may terminate the early-access DPA with 7 days' written notice.
- On termination Redwood will delete Partner Sandbox Data within 30 days unless Partner requests export/archive.
- Redwood will provide a data export in common formats (JSON/CSV) and a deletion certificate.

Limited liability (short form):
- Parties agree to a mutual cap for early-access activities prorated to the amount paid for the early-access program (if any).
- No warranty for model outputs; Partner uses sandbox outputs at their own risk.

Vendor security assessment checklist (for fast onboarding):
- Evidence request list (early-access):
  1) SOC 2 type II report OR completed self-attestation form.
  2) Network diagram for sandbox endpoints (obfuscated IPs allowed).
  3) Brief runbook for incident detection and primary contacts.
  4) Confirmation of TLS enforcement and cipher suite.
  5) Description of data deletion workflow for sandbox artifacts.
- Minimal questions to surface red flags:
  - Do you accept customer-managed keys for sandbox workloads? (Y/N)
  - Can you restrict operator access by customer project? (Y/N)
  - Are debug logs scrubbed of raw payloads by default? (Y/N)
  - Do you retain model prompts or full request payloads beyond 30 days? (Yes — explain)

Open items / negotiation points (for legal and security):
- Retention SLA for debug artifacts: standard 30 days but some partners request 90 days.
- Acceptable subprocessor objection process and escalation path.
- Format and level of detail for 24-hour breach notifications (first notice often incomplete).

Operational annex (quick-run checklist for onboarding engineers):
- Partner fills onboarding form: data classes + region pinning + contact emails + desired retention.
- Security team does quick evidence check using the 5-item list above.
- Provision sandbox with naming convention: ea-<partner>-<region>.
- Enable operator alerting and attach partner contact on-call for first 14 days.
- Schedule 1-week post-launch sync to review logs and tune sampling.

Drafting notes and next steps:
- This template is intentionally compact to remove friction for early integrations. Recommend Legal and Security review before use with regulated data.
- Row for full DPA mapping: convert minimal clauses into full DPA exhibits when partner transitions to production.
- TODOs: reconcile objection timeline with procurement (Maya K), draft minimal indemnity clause (Jon R), add example export manifest (Liam O).

References and links:
- Confluence: SEC-EARLY-ACCESS-DPA-2025 (stub)
- Jira: SEC-3421 (tracking onboarding playbook)

Notes to negotiators (internal):
- Be pragmatic: early-access partners are higher touch; prefer operational controls over heavy contract terms.
- Keep liability and warranty language short but ensure escalation for breaches.
- Preserve option to opt into full DPA for customers that become production.

Document history and versioning:
- v0.1 — initial draft for security/legal review (2025-02-10).
- v0.2 — to capture negotiation points and procurement feedback (target 2025-03-15).

Unresolved questions (quick list):
- Should 24-hour notification be absolute or limited to "confirmed material incidents"? (Security preference: notify all confirmed detections).
- Default log retention for sandbox: 30 vs 14 days for higher privacy.
- Does procurement accept the proposed 7-day termination window?

End of template.

-- internal editing notes --
Rationale: early-access partners need low friction onboarding. This DPA aims to allow product teams to iterate while preserving a minimum safe baseline for data handling. We expect to map this into the canonical DPA for production usage.
